title: The Cold War
examples: What were the main differences between the USA and the USSR?
How did the Cold War affect everyday life?
What caused the Berlin Wall to fall?

explain.say: The Cold War was a period of tension between two major powers. These powers were the United States and the Soviet Union.
The two sides had very different ideas about how countries should be run. The USA supported democracy and free markets. The USSR supported communism.
A key part of the tension was the arms race. Both sides built huge numbers of weapons. This created a constant state of military readiness.
The division of Berlin became a very visible symbol of this conflict. The Berlin Wall physically separated East and West Berlin.
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 was a major turning point. It symbolized the end of the Cold War division. This event was very significant.
In everyday life, the Cold War meant that many countries had to spend large amounts of money on defense. People lived under the shadow of potential conflict.

faq.q: Why was it called a Cold War?
faq.a: It was called cold because the two superpowers never engaged in direct, large-scale fighting. Instead, they fought through proxy wars and political tension.
asks: Was it a hot war or a cold war?

faq.q: What was the main disagreement between the USA and the USSR?
faq.a: The main disagreement was over political and economic systems. The USA promoted democracy while the USSR promoted communism.

faq.q: What was the purpose of the Berlin Wall?
faq.a: The Berlin Wall was built by East Germany to stop its citizens from escaping to West Berlin, which was controlled by the West.
asks: What did the wall keep people from seeing?

faq.a: In 1989, the Berlin Wall fell, which was a major public event. This event signaled the weakening of the Soviet Union's control.
asks: What happened to the wall in 1989?

faq.q: Did the Cold War end suddenly?
faq.a: No, the end was a process. The Soviet Union eventually collapsed in 1991, marking the end of the Cold War era.
asks: When did the Cold War really finish?
What followed the fall of the wall?

facts: The Cold War was primarily an ideological struggle between capitalism and communism.
The arms race involved the development and stockpiling of nuclear weapons.
The Berlin Wall separated East Berlin from West Berlin.
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 is seen as a major turning point.

quiz.say: The USA believed in which economic system?
quiz.why: Capitalism supports private ownership and free markets, which the USA championed.

wrong.0: This is an outdated system not related to the 20th-century conflict.
wrong.1: This was an older economic theory, not the basis of US policy.
wrong.3: This is the system the Soviet Union promoted, not the USA.

quiz.say: What did the arms race primarily involve?
quiz.why: The core fear was mutual destruction through advanced weaponry.

wrong.1: Trade was important, but the race was focused on military might.
wrong.2: Economic changes were secondary to the military buildup.
wrong.3: While technology advanced, the primary focus was weapons.

quiz.say: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 symbolized:

options.show: The start of a new war
options.say: The start of a new war

quiz.why: The wall represented the physical division maintained by the USSR.

wrong.0: While capitalism gained ground, the collapse was due to internal Soviet weakness.
wrong.2: The fall of the wall actually signaled a move towards more democratic systems.
wrong.3: The event is historically viewed as a period of reduced tension.
